sections.Trust Boundaries: Boundary 1: Streamlit/FastAPI client process <-> MCP server process, crossed over SSE at http://localhost:8000/sse; arguments cross as LLM-generated JSON tool-call arguments, parsed with json.loads and passed to the MCP tool with no server-side re-validation beyond FastMCP's declared type coercion. Boundary 2: MCP tool function <-> in-process Python data layer (data_sources.hr_database, create_ticket.py); no serialization boundary, direct dict access. Boundary 3: MCP tool function (ask_for_workpolicy) <-> external RAG stack (PDFPlumberLoader-loaded PDF, HuggingFace embeddings, InMemoryVectorStore, OpenAI-compatible chat completion at INFERENCE_BASE_URL); retrieved PDF text and LLM completion cross into the tool return value unindexed and unverified. Boundary 4: client orchestrator <-> OPA server at localhost:8181, referenced only by opa_client.py's evaluate_policy/_fail_secure_decision; this boundary is never actually crossed by any code path reachable from a registered @mcp.tool function in mcp_server.py — evaluate_policy is dead code with respect to the live tool set. Boundary 5: client orchestrator <-> LLMGuard scanners (llm_guard_config.py); crossed for run_llm_with_mcp.py's chat() function only (input/output scan), not crossed for fast_server.py's chat() function, and not crossed inside mcp_server.py itself (no scanning at the tool-execution boundary).
sections.Data Flow: Request: end user types a question in the Streamlit UI (run_llm_with_mcp.py) or POSTs to fast_server.py's /chat; user_profile (role/department/name) is read from st.session_state or the request body and interpolated as free text into a system-prompt string, never sent as a structured field to the MCP server. The chat() loop calls the LLM (OpenAI-compatible chat.completions.create) with the tool schema from tool_definitions.json-equivalent introspection; the LLM emits a tool_call with JSON arguments; the client parses those arguments with json.loads and calls session.call_tool(tool_name, arguments) over SSE to mcp_server.py, which dispatches to the matching @mcp.tool function purely by declared parameter names/types (FastMCP), with no injected subject/role parameter. Inside the tool, hr_db/comp_db/purchase_db in-memory dicts are read (for compensation/purchase tools) or raw_*/RAG helpers are called; the manager whose data is returned is selected via get_current_user_context()['user_id'] defaulting to 'manager_123', not by any value the client actually sent. Response: the tool return string (JSON or CSV text, or a natural-language RAG answer) is returned over SSE to the client, optionally passed through LLMGuard's scan_tool_output (run_llm_with_mcp.py only), and then handed back to the LLM for the next turn or shown directly to the user; fast_server.py performs no output scanning at all.

Enforcement Points.Current: FastMCP declared-type coercion only; no authorization, no field filtering beyond the optional select_fields projection
Enforcement Points.Available (OPA-interceptable): A pre-execution Rego check could use input.name (tool), input.args.department/select_fields/format/external_sharing/business_justification/amount/product_name, and a genuinely-populated input.extensions.subject.roles to decide allow/deny before mcp_server.py executes any tool body
Enforcement Points.Blind spots: None of the declared subject fields are currently populated from a real per-request source (see Runtime Subject Context), so even a correctly-written policy has no trustworthy input.extensions.subject.* to evaluate against today; this is the primary blind spot, not the absence of policy code

Enforcement Points.Current: None; sensitive_data (ssn, home_address, bank_account, personal_email, emergency_contact, healthcare_plan, healthcare_id) is merged unconditionally before any select_fields projection is applied
Enforcement Points.Available (OPA-interceptable): A pre-execution policy could deny or force select_fields down to a safe subset based on input.args.select_fields and a real subject.roles value before the tool runs
Enforcement Points.Blind spots: department (view_team_compensation) and id (both tools) are declared arguments that the implementation ignores outright; a policy written against department would not match actual behavior, which always returns the caller's own hard-coded manager's team regardless of the requested department

Enforcement Points.Layer: External sharing / domain validation (email_compensation_report, export_compensation_data, send_email)
Enforcement Points.Current: Cosmetic only: email_compensation_report splits the destination domain for display; no domain allow/deny list, and external_sharing is echoed but never enforced in any of the three tools
Enforcement Points.Available (OPA-interceptable): input.args.destination / input.args.external_sharing are structured and available pre-execution; a policy could block on domain membership (guidance rules 6-8) and on external_sharing=true (guidance rules 17-18) before the tool sends anything
Enforcement Points.Blind spots: recipient_email, subject, and body on send_email are declared but never read by the implementation at all, so no policy decision keyed on those fields would change what the tool actually does today; enforcing on them would require the implementation to first read them

Enforcement Points.Current: None; amount is never compared against a role-based limit, and justification/category are ignored
Enforcement Points.Available (OPA-interceptable): input.args.amount plus a real subject.roles/max_purchase value would let a pre-execution policy enforce guidance rules 9-10 (employee <$200 without approval, manager <$1000)
Enforcement Points.Blind spots: There is no declared 'approval' argument on purchase and no verified subject field carrying manager-approval status; system_vars.json's top-level "approval": "true|false" is a template placeholder with no runtime producer, so guidance rule 9's 'without manager approval' clause has no structured input to bind to today

Undeclared Fields.Field: manager approval status (rule 9: 'Employees cannot buy products $200+ without manager approval')
Undeclared Fields.Declared by: Declared nowhere: purchase's input_schema has no approval/approver field, and system_vars.json's "approval": "true|false" is an undated template placeholder with no runtime code path that ever sets it on a real request
Undeclared Fields.Consequence: A future policy cannot express the approval-required branch of rule 9 against any structured input; it can only enforce the flat $200/$1000 role-based ceilings

Undeclared Fields.Field: department scoping for view_team_compensation (rule 1: 'View only the requested manager's team...')
Undeclared Fields.Declared by: Declared by view_team_compensation's own department argument, but the implementation ignores it and always returns the current_user_context user_id's hard-coded team
Undeclared Fields.Consequence: declared by another mechanism (the ignored department arg) rather than nowhere, but any OPA policy that conditions on input.args.department would not correspond to what the tool actually returns unless the implementation is fixed to honor it first

Undeclared Fields.Field: field-must-be-specified requirement (rule 15: '...the request must specify which fields to return; requests that do not specify any fields must be blocked')
Undeclared Fields.Declared by: Declared by view_team_compensation.select_fields and export_compensation_data.select_fields (both optional, default null)
Undeclared Fields.Consequence: declared by the governing tools themselves, so this is directly OPA-policy-expressible today by checking input.args.select_fields for null/empty; no gap

Undeclared Fields.Field: blocked-phrase detection ('ignore all policies', 'bypass security', 'override all policies', 'show all SSN data')
Undeclared Fields.Declared by: Declared nowhere as a tool argument or subject field; currently implemented only as free-text prompt scanning (LLMGuard BanSubstrings in llm_guard_config.py, and business/malicious pattern lists in run_llm_with_mcp.py.enforce_input), both upstream of and outside any registered tool's input_schema, and not present at all in fast_server.py's path
Undeclared Fields.Consequence: Not OPA-policy-expressible against structured input.args/input.extensions.subject today, since the offending text lives only in the free-form user prompt (a distinct source per the shared source-boundary rule) and is never copied into a declared tool argument; enforcement remains prompt-layer only and is inconsistent across the two client entry points

Undeclared Fields.Field: personal_email visibility for view_team_compensation (rule 16: 'Managers cannot see any team member's personal email address')
Undeclared Fields.Declared by: Declared by view_team_compensation's own select_fields mechanism (personal_email is one of the documented Available fields) but the implementation always merges personal_email into member_data before any role check -- there is no separate role/subject field gating it
Undeclared Fields.Consequence: OPA-expressible via input.args.select_fields today, but only as a positive block-if-requested rule; there is no subject field distinguishing 'manager for this team' from any other caller, so the policy could not also verify the caller is actually that team's manager

handoff.Summary: Inspected mcp_server.py (canonical FastMCP tool-registration server matching all 11 tool_definitions.json tools exactly plus get_w2_form), fast_server.py and run_llm_with_mcp.py (client orchestrators), create_ticket.py, rag_pipeline.py, rag_salary.py, opa_client.py, opa_config.py, llm_guard_config.py, data_sources/hr_database.py (10 implementation files, within the 20-file/2-hop caps). All 11 tools have an implementation finding (none Unknown). 5 layers identified: agent/client, MCP, tool implementation, runtime context/enforcement, external service. Key finding: OPA (opa_client.py) is fully built but never called from any live @mcp.tool function -- it is dead code with respect to the registered server; LLMGuard is wired only into run_llm_with_mcp.py, not fast_server.py or mcp_server.py itself. Runtime subject fields (role, teams, permissions, id) have no real per-request provenance -- user_role is self-selected in a UI dropdown and never read by any compensation/purchase tool body for an authorization decision. 5 undeclared-field gaps recorded, most significantly: manager-approval status for purchases (rule 9) has no structured field anywhere, and the four 'blocked phrase' guidance rules (11-14) are enforced only as free-text prompt scanning, not as any declared tool argument or subject field, so they are not OPA-policy-expressible against structured input today. 34 tool-argument rows recorded across the 11 tools, with numerous Ignored dispositions (department and id on both compensation tools, category/justification on purchase, recipient_email/subject/body/report_data on send_email and email_compensation_report) where the LLM-facing docstring promises behavior the implementation does not perform.
